subtitle: Lesson 10 · Authentication for Integrations

code:
Standard HTTPS:                    Mutual TLS:
Server -> certificate -> Client    Server -> certificate -> Client
Client's identity proven            Client -> certificate -> Server
  separately (OAuth/Basic Auth)     Both sides verify before anything runs
caption: One-directional trust, versus both sides proving who they are.

code:
HTTP Headers on the REST Message:

X-API-Key: abc123xyz789

A static shared secret the external API recognizes —
no token endpoint, no OAuth profile, no expiration by default.
caption: Configured as a plain header, not an Authentication Profile.

steps.label: No standard spec
steps.sub: every vendor picks its own header name, format, and revocation process

steps.label: No built-in expiration
steps.sub: a leaked key stays valid until someone manually rotates it

steps.label: No scope model
steps.sub: usually all-or-nothing access, not limited to specific permissions

steps.label: OAuth
steps.sub: the default choice whenever the external system supports it

steps.label: Mutual TLS
steps.sub: when certificate-based verification on both ends is a hard requirement

steps.label: API key
steps.sub: when the partner simply offers nothing stronger
